- When sentiment turns bullish (↑) after a recent dip, model tends to overreact and overshoot — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After strong bullish sentiment spikes, model often overestimates continuation — apply downward correction if sentiment stabilizes or turns neutral.
- If sentiment is consistently bearish (↓) over 3+ days, model underestimates downside risk — add 2–5% buffer to forecast lows.
- Model tends to lag sentiment shifts — if sentiment turns bullish within 2 days, adjust forecast upward by 1–3% per day.
- When news volume drops below 2.0, model overcorrects — reduce forecast by 1–3% to align with muted market activity.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts often overestimate volatility — cap max deviation at ±5% from 30-day moving average.
